records.name: Turkey
records.summary_text: Turkey presents real, structured danger for trans visitors — institutionalised, presidential-level hostility that has become state policy. Police profile and detain trans women for identity checks (20 detained in Istanbul in July 2025), trans women have historically been frequent targets of torture and ill-treatment by police, and a trans woman attacked with a knife was herself detained (victim-criminalised). Transphobic attacks and Pride-event violence are documented, and foreign visitors must carry original passports at all times — creating outing risk at the frequent transit checkpoints.

records.name: Denmark
records.summary_text:
Denmark is a historically progressive destination. It was the first European country to introduce legal gender recognition by self-declaration (2014), has banned conversion therapy (2023), offers nonbinary gender markers, and has comprehensive anti-discrimination protections covering gender identity. There is no rollback movement, and Copenhagen ranks among the world's most LGBTQ+-welcoming cities.

One documented visitor-relevant weakness: the Danish Institute for Human Rights flags that police under-investigate hate crimes and are not obliged to flag hate-crime motivation at the time
